learning_outcomes.text: The student must demonstrate knowledge, understanding, and the ability to describe the basic concepts related to theoretical computer science, computer architecture, and high-level programming languages.
The student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of programs for solving problems of limited complexity.
The student must demonstrate the ability to apply the learned knowledge to solve simple programming problems, designing and developing programs for problems of limited complexity.

syllabus_topics: The concept of processing and algorithm
Finite state automata: definition, graph, and table
Boolean algebra: definitions and De Morgan's theorem
Representation of natural, relative, and real numbers
Fundamentals of computer system architecture: the Von Neumann model, processor operation
The life cycle of a program
Fundamentals of programming: simple and structured data types; elementary instructions and control structures
Abstract data types: lists, stacks, queues
Use of a program development environment with examples of fundamental algorithms and abstract data type management
teaching_methods: Practical exercises on C++ program development (40% of total hours)
Exercises in the classroom and/or laboratory with an integrated development environment and virtual didactic laboratory platforms
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a programming test on the computer and an oral exam. The outcome of the programming test is binding for access to the oral exam.
bibliography: Chianese, V. Moscato, A. Picariello, C. Sansone: Le radici dell’Informatica: dai bit alla programmazione strutturata, Maggioli Editore, 2017.
